# Summary {.unnumbered}

```{python}
#| include: false
from cohort_common import *
usable_results = rule_results(WATER_MIN, CENTRE_MIN)               # only the water-rich scans
rejected_results = rule_results(WATER_MIN, CENTRE_MIN, rejected=True)  # only the rejected, fatty scans
every_results = rule_results(-np.inf, -np.inf)                     # every scan

def share(results):
    higher, total, _ = results["CANCER vs NORMAL"]
    return f"{higher / total:.0%}", f"{higher}/{total}"

higher, compared, _ = usable_results["CANCER vs NORMAL"]
interval = binomtest(higher, compared).proportion_ci(method="exact")
```

::: {.summary-lead}
Human 1.0 shows that the difference between NORMAL and CANCER breasts is in the **water-rich scans**. Measured there, a basic analysis points to
the CANCER breast rather than the NORMAL one, matching synchrotron and ex-vivo data on the water-rich side.
:::

::: {.summary-expect}
**What we expect:** a normal breast is mostly fat with some glandular/fibrous tissue. Cancer replaces fat with cells and remodelled fibrous tissue,
which hold more water. Each breast gets one number, its **Water:Fat ratio**: the area of its water peak divided by the area of its fat peak, from
two fitted Gaussians. Comparing a patient's two breasts, the **CANCER breast should have the higher Water:Fat**.
:::

::: {.summary-data}
**Data:** **`{python} len(patient_novas)`** patients analysed with Human 1.0 (NORMAL, BENIGN or CANCER); **`{python} len(analysis_novas)`** used,
after leaving out `{python} len(patient_novas) - len(analysis_novas)` with a large left/right intensity imbalance ([Appendix I](intensity.qmd)).
:::

::: {.summary-row .two}
::: {.summary-card .glandular}
[1. The difference is in the water-rich scans]{.summary-label}

In the **fattiest 15%** of samples the three cohorts look the same; in the **wettest 15%** they separate NORMAL &lt; BENIGN &lt; CANCER. The
information is in the water-rich tissue — denser breasts are better for us; mammography's weakness is our strength
([Chapter 1](water_rich.qmd)).
:::

::: {.summary-card}
[2. It matches other data]{.summary-label}

That wettest-15% ordering matches synchrotron and Keele ex-vivo data. A fixed water-peak threshold for single-point scans
([Appendix C](the_rule.qmd)) also keeps the wet tissue; the paired test there supports CANCER vs NORMAL
([Chapter 2](other_data.qmd)).
:::

::: {.summary-card}
[3. Rigorous tumour targeting is not needed]{.summary-label}

The tumours are small and only a few beams are placed approximately, yet the signal holds where the beam goes through glandular tissue: changes
appear wide-reaching in the glandular breast, not confined to the tumour ([Chapter 3](tumour.qmd)).
:::

::: {.summary-card .recommended}
[4. Mapping for Human 2.0]{.summary-label} [Proposal]{.summary-badge}

Scan a grid over the whole breast and select the wettest tissue after the scan. The water-peak rule ([Appendix C](the_rule.qmd)) could be a
stopgap on Human 1.0; mapping is the recommendation ([Chapter 4](mapping.qmd)).
:::
:::

```{python}
#| label: fig-summary-examples
#| fig-cap: "**Top**: water-rich scans (usable). **Bottom**: fatty scans the rule rejects. Each panel is one patient; each curve the mean of that breast's scans of that kind. On water-rich scans the CANCER breast stands out; on fatty scans NORMAL/NORMAL and NORMAL/CANCER look alike."
# top row: both breasts usable; bottom row: both breasts have rejected (fatty) scans only
EXAMPLES = ((266, False), (439, False), (506, True), (250, True))  # (nova, use rejected scans)
found_use = rule_breasts(WATER_MIN, CENTRE_MIN)
found_rej = rule_breasts(WATER_MIN, CENTRE_MIN, rejected=True)
plt.rcParams["font.size"] = 7
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(8, 5.2), sharex=True, sharey=True)
for ax, (nova, rejected) in zip(axes.flat, EXAMPLES):
    found = found_rej if rejected else found_use
    labels = []
    for side, style in (("LEFT", "-"), ("RIGHT", "--")):
        label, ratio, n_kept, _ = found[nova, side]
        curves = [curve for n, s, _, curve, height, centre in scan_records
                  if n == nova and s == side and usable(height, centre, WATER_MIN, CENTRE_MIN) != rejected]
        with warnings.catch_warnings():
            warnings.simplefilter("ignore", RuntimeWarning)
            ax.plot(q, np.nanmean(curves, axis=0), color=ne.STATUS_COLOURS[label], ls=style, lw=1.6,
                    label=f"{side} {label}, Water:Fat {ratio:.2f}")
        labels.append(label)
    ax.axvspan(*WATER, color="grey", alpha=0.12, lw=0)
    ax.hlines(WATER_MIN, *WATER, color="black", lw=1.5, zorder=5)
    kind = "fatty scans" if rejected else "water-rich scans"
    ax.set(title=f"{' / '.join(labels)}: {kind}", xlim=(2, 25))
    ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
    ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=6, loc="upper left")
for ax in axes[-1]:
    ax.set_xlabel("q (nm⁻¹)")
for ax in axes[:, 0]:
    ax.set_ylabel("I(q), prepared")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
plt.rcParams["font.size"] = 10
```

::: {.summary-caveat}
**A pilot result:** `{python} compared` CANCER/NORMAL patients, 95% CI `{python} f"{interval.low:.0%}–{interval.high:.0%}"`, and mostly dense
breasts. All limitations are in [Chapter 5](limitations.qmd).
:::
